newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes just firmer, looks for bounce.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes just firmer, looks for bounce.

text.p: Gold dealers on Thursday were looking for the bullion market to continue the bounce from the 4-1/4 year low it plumbed the previous day.
But with sentiment remaining overwhelmingly bearish, the response would be limited, several dealers said.
Gold fixed at $332.30 per ounce, against a previous $332.15 and the $331.45 struck on Wednesday morning, which was the lowest since March 24, 1993.
"We are looking for a bounce from the current level but expect to see resistance at $334.00," one dealer said.
The return of Hong Kong to the market after being closed all week for the territory's transfer to Chinese rule brought additional interest to gold.
"Undoubtedly Hong Kong being closed this week took some demand out of the market," a dealer said.

Short covering was evident in the former British colony and in Tokyo during Far East trading but that was countered by selling from Australian producers. "Any producer selling now is doing so under pressure," a dealer said.
Technically gold was oversold with a Relative Strength Index of 29 to support the idea that it was ready to consolidate or even firm up.
The well discounted decision of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) not to push for a rise in U.S. interest rates yesterday had little market impact.
Some dealers thought the investment funds that were holding large short positions in gold might be tempted to cover at least some of these holdings before the U.S. Independence Day holiday on Friday.
Others said it was more likely the funds would wait to comfirm market direction before making a move.
"We are looking for the market to climb back to $336/$338," one dealer said.
Silver was barely a cent easier at $4.64/$4.66, having attracted little attention or attempted to shadow moves in gold.
"Silver has to hold $4.60," a dealer said, referring to a level that has held several times so far this year.
Platinum and palladium were also little changed from Wednesday as the markets awaited Russia's first exports of the year now due on July 10.
Platinum was indicated at $423.00/$427.00, barely changed, and palladium was $2.00 lower at $188.00/$193.00.
